Definition: properly, fusion, i.e. literally, a casting (of metal); figuratively, a mass (of clay)
BiblicalUsage: Mutsaq is a casting, a thing poured and hardened — the molten sea is cast in one piece, ten cubits from brim to brim, the ten bases are of one casting, and the dust grows into hardness when the clods cleave fast together.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the casting is the picture of work done once and done well: poured, hardened, and standing for generations.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
